cases.question: Our 6-year-old monolith handles 80% of company revenue. Velocity has dropped — new features take 3-4x longer than estimates. The eng leadership is split between a 12-month full rewrite, a 6-month bounded refactor, and a continuous-incremental strategy. We have 18 engineers and a 9-month runway before our Series B. Rank these options and name the conditions under which the ranking flips.

We're moving off self-managed Postgres on EC2. Options: (a) RDS, (b) Aurora, (c) a hosted-Postgres specialist like Crunchy or Neon. Workload: 800 GB OLTP plus a 2 TB analytics replica. We have one Postgres expert on staff. Pick one and name the tripwire.

A senior engineer is the world-class expert on one critical subsystem but has actively damaged team morale over 12 months — multiple junior engineers have quit citing them. Performance interventions have not changed behaviour. Options: (a) keep them and partition the team, (b) fire them and absorb the bus-factor risk, (c) try a final structured PIP. Rank with explicit conditions for switching.
